title: Minimum fill-in

problem.name: Minimum fill-in
problem.statement_latex:
Given $G=(V,E)$, minimize $|F|$ over added-edge sets $F\subseteq\binom V2\setminus E$ such that $(V,E\cup F)$ is chordal, meaning every cycle of length at least four has a chord. Minimum fill-in controls additional nonzero entries created by sparse elimination.
The quantum ordering bound uses QRAM time, while the classical structural algorithm uses RAM time on the explicit graph.
problem.statement_text: Given $G=(V,E)$, minimize $|F|$ over added-edge sets $F\subseteq\binom V2\setminus E$ such that $(V,E\cup F)$ is chordal, meaning every cycle of length at least four has a chord. Minimum fill-in controls additional nonzero entries created by sparse elimination. The quantum ordering bound uses QRAM time, while the classical structural algorithm uses RAM time on the explicit graph.

quantum.details_latex: An elimination order determines a chordal completion by making each eliminated vertex's remaining neighborhood a clique. The ordering recurrence charges the newly inserted edges and optimizes the total cost. Partial preprocessing and quantum minimum finding provide the stated bound with exponential coherent memory.
quantum.details_text: An elimination order determines a chordal completion by making each eliminated vertex's remaining neighborhood a clique. The ordering recurrence charges the newly inserted edges and optimizes the total cost. Partial preprocessing and quantum minimum finding provide the stated bound with exponential coherent memory.

classical.details_latex: The algorithm enumerates potential maximal cliques and minimal-separator blocks, then selects compatible triangulations with minimum fill cost. Its time improves on the generic $O^*(2^n)$ elimination-order recurrence, and its space is exponential. The graph structure exploited by this method gives the smaller base in the overall comparison.

strength.description_latex: The classical $1.7347^n$ bound is asymptotically smaller than the displayed quantum $1.817^n$ bound. The quantum result accelerates the subset-ordering recurrence.

evidence.description_latex: The ordering acceleration has a rigorous upper bound; the strongest displayed overall complexity bound is classical.

hardware.description_latex: The quantum construction requires polynomial active subset and fill-cost registers with exponential QRAM. Useful depths require fault tolerance. The stronger classical structural method also uses exponential storage.
